text.p: Portuguese bonds closed at their day's highs but failed to rise as strongly as their Spanish and Italian equivalents and dealers said profit-taking and concern over U.S. hourly earnings data had put a lid on gains.

"The mood is much more positive. Liquidity has increased and we finished at around the day's highs," said one dealer. "But although U.S. non-farm payrolls were benign, hourly earnings have raised worries about a rise in U.S. rates."
Other traders said shorter maturities were still enjoying support from a belief that the Bank of Portugal will cut its key rates soon, possibly next week. -- Lisbon editorial +(351-1) 3538254
